title: Hurricane Florence Disaster Relief
description: Zachary Hierl, a paramedic with Onslow County EMS and a member of Onslow County Swift Fire rescue team, provides an interview regarding recovery efforts in Jacksonville, N.C., Sept. 16, 2018. Marines from across II Marine Expeditionary Force and Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune are assisting with disaster relief efforts for those affected by strong winds, heavy rain, power outages, and flooded housing due to Hurricane Florence. Hurricane Florence, with its heavy rain and strong winds, is the biggest storm to hit the Carolinas since Hurricane Floyd in 1999, causing power outages and flooding damages and forcing many first responders to be ready at a moment's notice. (U.S. Marine Corps video by Lance Cpl. Leynard Plazo)
keywords: CLB-8, disaster relief, Camp Lejeune, Hurricane Florence, hurricaneflorece, Marines, North Carolina, Jacksonville

transcript.text: Over the last couple days in the wake of Hurricane Florence, we have been responding to multiple calls for
swift water rescues as well as people trapped in their homes needing assistance and being evacuated
to local shelters. Joint efforts with the Marines has been absolutely phenomenal. We are having that
great relationship with the base and the county. It's beneficial to all the citizens in Oslo County
and being able to team up together to get out and help those in need. Just people in our community
that need our help has been absolutely awesome and I think it's been amazing. The trucks have
been a huge help to access places that we couldn't access before knowing that when they call for help
help is coming. It's got to be a big morale booster for them and we wouldn't be able to we would not
have been able to facilitate that ourselves without the help of the Marine Corps. These these are our
people so this is this is where we want to be and who we want to be helping the most is our neighbors
and our friends and our families.
